top_categories.workout_context: 205 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
At Race Across Italy 300, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
15,092ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
74ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Race Across Italy 300's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before May.

Road-specific control matters at Race Across Italy 300. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 205 miles.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 205 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
205 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 15,092ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Race Across Italy 300. Train it until it feels boring.
15,092ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Low-cadence force work supports 15,092ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

race_overlay.weather: May in Silvi Paese, Teramo, Italy — Early May in Abruzzo -- coastal start, climbing into the Apennine foothills; expect cool mornings and variable conditions over an 18-20 hour effort. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking before Race Across Italy 300. Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 205 miles: 80–100g carbs/hour from mile 1 — don’t wait until you’re hungry. Practice your exact race-day nutrition in every long training ride. Carry backup calories. 205 miles burns 8,000–12,000+ calories — you cannot replace them all, but you must try.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Race Across Italy 300. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Race Across Italy 300 rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Over Under, and Mixed Climbing to prepare you for 205 miles of mixed terrain in Silvi Paese, Teramo, Italy.
